items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Then after Stuff, the next name I worked with was Roy Eldridge and Sonny Stitt.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, see, Roy come to Chicago looking for a band, and he knew Stitt was hanging around, because I think that's where Eckstein's band broke up was in Chicago; in fact, they did break up in Chicago. They played the Regal Theatre and that was the end of it. But Stitt was around then, and he told me one night, it was at a little after hours place, all the musicians used to come and jam,

called 'Slappy's' on 29th and Indiana. And after I got off my job downtown on Sunday, I'd pull by there. You know, and we just jammed all morning, to at least 1 or 2 o'clock in the afternoon. And Stitt would be down there, and he says to me, 'Man, I got a job for you if you want it.' He had [Don Rail] Anderson drumming, a pianist named Willie Jones, who, Willie incidentally, was playing that locked-hand style, and still is, Big Willie Jones -- he said you're going to work with Roy Eldridge. Elton: Roy had 2 weeks…
So we bought uniform jackets at least, and we went to Milwaukee with Roy Elton.
